ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended), Enforcement Decree No. 17816, as amended; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality (Act No. 5493, as amended); Financial Services Commission's Customer Identification and Beneficial Ownership Guidelines; FATF Recommendations 10, 24 and 25 as implemented by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU). Korea does not operate a publicly searchable UBO register; beneficial ownership information is collected under the AML/CFT customer due diligence framework and disclosed only to KoFIU and other competent government authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Company Incorporation (Commercial Registration Certificate issued from the court commercial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Division, District Court of Seoul
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public, then either (1) Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Apostille member states, or (2) MOFA authentication followed by consular legalization at the diplomatic mission of the destination non-member state in Seoul. The Hague and consular routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Business Registration (Business Tax Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public, then either Hague Apostille by MOFA (Apostille member states) or MOFA authentication plus consular legalization by the destination state's embassy/consulate in Seoul (non-member states). The two authentication paths are alternatives, not sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of No Tax Default / Good Standing of the Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public, followed by a single exclusive authentication route: Hague Apostille by MOFA for member states or MOFA authentication plus consular legalization for non-member states. Do not apply both paths to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Articles of Association (Jung-gwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public, with registry-confirmed filing number
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, then mutually exclusive option of Hague Apostille (MOFA) or consular legalization (MOFA authentication plus destination consulate). Apostille and consular legalization are alternative completions and cannot be layered.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) board of directors, certified by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized board resolution, then either Hague Apostille by MOFA for all Apostille Convention jurisdictions or, exclusively for non-members, MOFA authentication and consular legalization by the destination country's consular post in Seoul.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank with regulated presence in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The original letter is sealed by the bank's compliance office; where the receiving jurisdiction requires it, the sealed original is notarized and then completed solely through either a Hague Apostille (MOFA) or consular legalization (MOFA authentication plus destination consulate), according to the receiving state's status under the Apostille Convention.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover every shareholder, director, 25% or more beneficial owner, and any individual with management authority. The compliance protocol requires continuous PEP and family/close-associate checks against KoFIU, FATF and global PEP databases; OFAC SDN and SSI list screening; the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; EU consolidated sanctions; and Korean domestic sanctions and alert lists. All hits must be risk-assessed, and PEPs automatically trigger enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Results must be documented and retained for five years under the Specific Financial Transaction Information Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-Registry / IREOS) and the Commercial Registration Information System operated by the local District Court Commercial Registration Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name must be registered in Hangul. A foreign or English transliteration may be recorded only as a supplementary name in the articles of association, and the Korean statutory liability suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' must appear in the official Hangul name. Names follow a four-tier structure: (1) distinctive element, (2) optional description of business scope, (3) statutory corporate-form suffix, and (4) registered-office municipal designation. Romanized transliteration must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean, and no name may be confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name or imply a governmental, financial, or public institution.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection with the head of the district court registry demanding correction within seven days of the rejection. If the registry head dismisses the objection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the appellate court within 14 days under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The appeal must identify the rejected name, the statutory basis for distinctiveness, and the removal of prohibited tokens. A further re-appeal to the Supreme Court may be filed within seven days. Alternatively, the applicant may expedite incorporation by amending the name and refiling a new application, while preserving the original rejection record.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is categorically rejected for a Yuhan Hoesa operating a delivery-only ghost kitchen facility. The Food Sanitation Act requires a food service business report or license to identify the exact physical location of the cooking, storage, and delivery preparation premises. The municipal government issuing the license and the local district tax office require that the registered office correspond to an actual leasable commercial kitchen. Korean banks also reject virtual-office domiciles for business account opening because the anti-money laundering customer due diligence process requires documentary proof of physical premises and often an on-site visit. Use of a virtual office would invalidate the food service license, block tax registration, and jeopardize payment rails such as UberEats and DoorDash payouts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated quantified risk: greater than 80% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months after license issuance for a ghost kitchen operator. Checklist for readiness: (1) business registration certificate visibly posted; (2) kitchen layout matches the licensed floor plan; (3) food hygiene and cold-chain logs; (4) waste disposal and sewerage contracts; (5) fire extinguishers and safety permits; (6) employee labor and immigration records; (7) sub-lease or shared-kitchen authorization; (8) cash register and POS transaction records. Registry and municipal inspectors may coordinate with the tax office; any mismatch is treated as a license violation exposing the company to fines, closure orders, or revocation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 543, 545, 546, 548, 553, 554, 555, 557, 558, 559, 562 and 563; Commercial Registration Act Articles 34 to 36; Act on the Regulation of Tax Invoice Issuance and Electronic Transactions, Article 16
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registry Bureau; for filing purposes the district court registry office (Corporate Registry Section) having jurisdiction over the registered office, in Seoul being the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), together with notarized Articles of Incorporation and the capital deposit certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital exists under the Korean Commercial Act. However, the full subscribed capital must be contributed before the registration application is filed, and the founders must obtain a bank capital deposit certificate or certified savings passbook evidencing that the capital is held in a designated corporate bank account in the name of the company. No separate escrow account is required, but released funds are restricted to incorporation expenses and must remain unwithdrawn until the registration is formally completed. In-kind contributions must be appraised and stated in the Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY), ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 555 OF THE KOREAN COMMERCIAL ACT AND ARTICLE 3 OF THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION.

WHEREAS, the Company has been organized as a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) under the Commercial Act of South Korea for the purpose of operating delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen facilities; and

WHEREAS, it is necessary to establish the capital structure, banking mandate, registered office, statutory officers and corporate governance in compliance with the Korean Commercial Act and subordinate regulations; and

WHEREAS, the directors and the sole member have determined that the initial actions required by the registration procedure shall be authorized by this resolution.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION. Each initial subscriber shall subscribe and pay in full the contribution set forth in the capital subscription schedule. The Chief Executive Officer shall receive the paid-in capital, open a dedicated corporate bank account in the name of the Company, obtain a bank capital deposit certificate, and preserve all funds in such account until the Company incorporation registration is completed. No portion of the subscribed capital may be withdrawn except for pre-registration incorporation expenses authorized by the Board.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board and its authorized officers are hereby empowered and directed to execute any banking resolutions, signature cards, electronic transfer mandates and wire instructions necessary to open, maintain and operate the Company primary operating bank account. Such officers may connect the account to digital payment and delivery platform payout systems, including UberEats and DoorDash, and may execute any agreements, schedules, and settlement instruments with such platforms. The Chairperson, the Chief Executive Officer, and the Chief Financial Officer, any two acting jointly, are designated as authorized signatories.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company shall be located at the address stipulated in the Articles of Incorporation, and the Chief Executive Officer is authorized to execute the lease agreement, register the office with the Business Registration Office of the National Tax Service and the corporate registry, and furnish any required lease consents from the landlord.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board elects and appoints the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, and the Compliance and Food Safety Officer. Each officer shall have authority to prepare, notarize, sign, stamp and file all formation documents, official registers, tax filings, and regulatory licensing applications, and to appear before government agencies. All such officers are required to comply with the Korean Commercial Act and the fiduciary duties applicable to directors and statutory officers.

5. GENERAL IMPLEMENTATION. The directors and officers are authorized to take such further actions as are necessary to obtain the corporate seal certificate, the food service business report, the fire safety inspection approval, environmental discharge permits, and insurance policies, and to incur reasonable establishment expenses not exceeding thirty million Korean won without further resolution.

6. EFFECTIVE DATE. This resolution shall be effective immediately upon execution and shall remain binding on the Company, all directors, officers, successors and assignees. A certified copy of this resolution shall be inserted into the Company minute book and filed after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Verification and Drafting of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr) and the local district court registry office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search using the corporate name database of the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office to ensure that the proposed corporate name of the Yuhan Hoesa is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company in the Republic of Korea. After clearance, draft the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language, stating the corporate name, the registered office address in South Korea, the business purpose including delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen operations, the capital contribution schedule, the number of directors, and the accounting period. The Articles of Incorporation must be executed by each founding member and should include a statement that no statutory minimum capital is required, while confirming the actual amount subscribed.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Capital subscription schedule signed by each founding member
Identification documents or passports of founding members
Written appointment of local registered agent or director, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as confusingly similar, withdraw the name application and amend the Articles of Incorporation by substituting a new distinctive corporate name, then resubmit the name search through the IRO. If the registry requests further identification or translation, provide notarized translations within two weeks; if the application remains suspended, a formal written statement of correction and a fresh filing may be submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public commissioned by the High Court, and any commercial bank authorized to operate in South Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend in person before a Korean notary with the final executed Articles of Incorporation and all founder identification. The notary will verify the subscribers signatures, the capacity of each founder, and the legality of the corporate purpose. After notarization, open a temporary corporate capital deposit account in the name of the Yuhan Hoesa with a licensed commercial bank and deposit the full subscribed capital. The bank must issue a capital deposit certificate or a certified savings passbook evidencing the balance and the account owner. If any contribution is made in kind, obtain an independent valuation report and attach it to the Articles of Incorporation before notarization.
required_dossiers: Final notarized Articles of Incorporation
Original identification of all subscribers and directors
Capital deposit certificate or certified passbook issued by the bank
In-kind asset valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to certify the Articles of Incorporation, correct the stated legal form or capital schedule and re-execute in a second session. If the bank requests additional anti-money-laundering documentation for the beneficial owners, provide source-of-funds declarations and corporate structure charts; if the capital deposit certificate is insufficient, request a replacement certificate with the official bank seal and re-submit within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Division, Seoul Central District Court Registry Office or the district court registry having jurisdiction over the registered office in South Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of incorporation with the competent district court registry office within thirty days after notarization and capital contribution. Submit the prescribed registration application form together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, written consents of the directors and any auditor appointed, the certificate of a corporate seal, a copy of the registered office lease or proof of right to use the premises, and a power of attorney for the local filing agent. The registry will review the documents, verify the address and paid-in capital, and, if satisfied, enter the company into the commercial register and issue a certificate of registered matters.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate or certified bank records
Written consents of directors and auditor, if any
Corporate seal report and seal certificate
Copy of registered office lease or landlord consent
Power of attorney and identification of the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension notice, respond within two weeks with a written correction, refile any defective pages, and pay the required fee. If the application is rejected due to defective capital proof, obtain a corrected bank certificate and submit a supplemental filing. If the court refuses registration, the applicant may apply for a review or appeal to the Supreme Court Registry Bureau.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Electronic Invoice Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) using the HomeTax online portal (www.hometax.go.kr) and the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly formed Yuhan Hoesa with the Korean tax authority for value added tax purposes before business commencement. Use the HomeTax portal to complete the business registration application, inserting the corporate legal name, corporate registration number, business address, date of business commencement, and business code corresponding to ISIC 5610. Attach the certificate of corporate registration, Articles of Incorporation, lease contract, corporate seal certificate, and identification of the representative. The NTS will assign a business registration number and issue a business registration certificate. Then register the corporate bank account with the NTS and apply for authorized tax invoice issuance privileges so that delivery platform payouts from UberEats and DoorDash can be documented and reconciled.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Certificate of corporate registration
Corporate seal certificate
Registered office lease contract or rent agreement
Representative identification and passport copy
Bank account designation form and proof of corporate account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS requests additional information, respond within ten days through HomeTax with supplementary evidence. If the tax office disputes the business place, submit a copy of the kitchen lease, floor plan, utility bill, and a landlord confirmation letter. If the application is suspended or rejected, file a correction with the district tax office or submit an objection to the National Tax Service within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Service Business Report and Local Facility Inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Food Hygiene Division of the competent autonomous district (gu) office, operating within the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a food service business report under Article 46 of the Food Sanitation Act with the local gu office before commencing ghost kitchen operations. The report must identify the company, the facility address, the representative, and the mode of business as delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen. Submit a scaled floor plan showing the receiving area, food preparation and cooking lines, refrigerated storage, separate hand-washing sinks, ventilation hoods, sanitary facilities, and waste collection points. The local public health inspector may visit the premises to verify structural compliance and the presence of protective and safety equipment. Once passed, the gu office issues the food service business report certificate, which is the statutory operating license for the ghost kitchen. All virtual brand names operated out of the kitchen must be recorded to avoid unauthorized trading under one license.
required_dossiers: Food service business report form
Business registration certificate issued by the NTS
Corporate registration certificate
Premises lease and landlord permission
Scaled floor plan of the kitchen facility
Food hygiene education certificate for the manager or responsible person
Civil defense and fire safety inspection certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gu office refuses or conditions the report on remedial works, complete the required renovations within the given correction period and apply for reinspection. If the facility fails the health inspection, submit a corrective action plan, schedule reinspection, and pay any required administrative fee. If the report is rejected after due process, the company may seek administrative review with the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety or appeal to the Administrative Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) through local autonomous district (gu) offices for food service licensing; Korea Fire Safety Authority (KOFIS) and local fire stations for fire safety; Ministry of Environment and Korea Environment Corporation for wastewater and air discharge registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Business Report Certificate for Delivery-Only Restaurant / Ghost Kitchen under Article 46 of the Food Sanitation Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) through the local environmental management office and Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier 2 Environmental Registration (notification) for a small standalone ghost kitchen; full Environmental Impact Assessment is Not Applicable unless the project involves a new building or extension with total floor area exceeding 100,000 square meters or falls under Schedule 1 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; a small-scale environmental assessment may be triggered only in specific high-protection land-planning zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The ghost kitchen must install a grease trap and comply with municipal sewer effluent limits if connected to public sewerage; typical local sewer limits for restaurant wastewater in Korea include pH 5.8 to 8.6, biochemical oxygen demand not exceeding 300 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 300 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 300 mg/L, and oil or n-hexane extracts not exceeding 90 mg/L. If wastewater is discharged directly into a water body without connection to a public sewer, the stricter Water Environment Conservation Act standards apply, generally limiting BOD and COD to 50 mg/L, TSS to 50 mg/L, total nitrogen to 60 mg/L, and total phosphorus to 8 mg/L. Cooking fumes and odors must be filtered by high-efficiency exhaust hoods and odor-control equipment to prevent nuisance under the Malodor Prevention Act, with volatile organic compound abatement as required by local air quality permits where installed capacity exceeds exemption thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must obtain fire safety approval under the Fire Safety Installation and Maintenance Act, including inspection of fire extinguishers, sprinklers, emergency exits, automatic fire detection systems, and fire-resistant compartmentation; after installation, a completion inspection is conducted by the Korea Fire Safety Authority or the local fire station. Civil Defense registration is required for emergency planning, including an evacuation route, shelter designation, and business continuity plan. The occupational licensing side requires compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, appointment of a workplace safety and health manager where applicable, risk assessment for hot-oil cooking hazards, electrical safety, ventilation system maintenance, and delivery-service worker safety protocols, all of which must be documented and kept available during government inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing and registration through the HomeTax electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr; customs export clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity engaging in Korean domestic business, the entity must first confirm whether it has a domestic place of business or Korean-source taxable income. If there is no fixed domestic place of business, it must appoint a domestic tax representative under Korean tax law who will receive tax documents, issue and receive tax invoices, and represent the entity before the NTS. The non-resident entity must prepare corporate formation documentation, including certified or apostilled articles of incorporation, a certificate of foreign business registration or equivalent corporate existence certificate, a board resolution appointing the domestic tax representative, a power of attorney, and identity documents for the representative. The application for business registration must be filed through HomeTax or in person at the district tax office having jurisdiction over the Korean place of business, using the standard non-resident foreign corporation business registration procedure. Upon validation of the foreign corporate existence, the domestic place of business, and the tax representative appointment, the NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number which serves as both the statutory Tax Identification Number for corporate income tax purposes and the Value-Added Tax registration number. After obtaining the Business Registration Number, the entity must activate the electronic tax invoice system through HomeTax or a certified value-added network service provider, open a Korean won foreign exchange bank account for settlement of export proceeds, and file quarterly VAT returns and annual corporate tax returns in accordance with Korean statutory deadlines. A foreign entity that has no Korean place of business but is eligible to claim a VAT refund may be registered through its Korean tax representative under the foreign non-resident VAT refund registration regime, but ordinary business registration applies when the entity actually operates a Korean trade or business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not operate a US-style check-the-box election nor a general pass-through election for Yuhan Hoesa. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is per se a domestic corporation subject to entity-level taxation under the Korean Corporate Tax Act, and its income is not treated as pass-through to shareholders. Hybrid mismatch rules are addressed on a mandatory statutory basis, not through elective mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None. Korean VAT law requires registration by every person engaged in a business activity as defined under the VAT Act, without a general turnover-based exemption threshold for corporations. Registration must be completed within 20 days after business commencement. The simplified taxable person status is available only to eligible small individual businesses and does not remove the obligation to register; it is not available to a limited liability company.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea does not employ a real-time fiscal pre-clearance stamping model. All business-to-business supplies must be documented through the mandatory electronic tax invoice (ETI) system, and invoices must be submitted in XML form to the NTS through HomeTax or a certified VAN provider using NTS-integrated interfaces. The electronic tax invoice must be issued no later than the last day of the month following the supply for ordinary quarterly filing, and transmission to the NTS must occur within the statutory filing deadlines. There is no per-transaction anti-fraud digital seal, but the NTS uses the ETI data, cash receipt reporting for business-to-consumer supplies, customs export declarations, and foreign exchange settlement records for automated cross-verification and audit targeting.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods exported from Korea by filing an export declaration with Korea Customs Service and to supplies of services rendered to foreign recipients where the place of supply is deemed outside Korea under the Korean VAT Act, including qualifying international services and digital services supplied to non-resident recipients. The taxpayer must prove that the goods were physically exported or that the services were actually supplied to a foreign counterparty, that the consideration in foreign currency was received from the foreign buyer, and that the applicable statutory export documentation has been preserved. For the ghost-kitchen and virtual-brand commercial model, local Korean delivery sales through platform payouts are standard-rated at 10%; zero-rating is available only for the physical export of packaged food products, or the cross-border licensing of virtual brand intellectual property or digital content to foreign non-resident buyers, provided those supplies satisfy the Korean VAT place-of-supply and export evidence requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration and export clearance certificate issued through the UNI-PASS system
Bill of Lading for ocean freight or Air Waybill for airfreight evidencing physical export from Korea
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank proving receipt of export proceeds
Customs broker authorization or power of attorney if export clearance is undertaken through an agent
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service jointly cross-match export declarations, electronic tax invoices, bills of lading, and foreign exchange settlement records. If a zero-rated export is found to be unsupported, fraudulent, or invalid because the goods never left Korea, the services were not supplied to a foreign recipient, or export proceeds were not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period without an approved extension, the NTS will disallow the zero-rating and assess VAT at 10% on the full supply, together with interest for underpaid tax. Additional tax penalties apply under Korean VAT law, including up to 20% for negligent non-filing or understatement and up to 40% for fraudulent evasion. Deliberate use of false export declarations, fabricated transport documents, or fictitious foreign recipients triggers criminal liability under the Act on the Punishment of Tax Evaders, with possible imprisonment and fines, in addition to retrospective clawback of any VAT refunds previously issued. The general tax assessment statute of limitations is 5 years, extended to 10 years for fraud or deliberate concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting through the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Foreign Exchange Operations Team under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with daily administration delegated to authorized foreign exchange banks
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a dual-account framework governed by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The won is fully convertible on the current account, including trade-related payments, invoicing for exported services, and profit remittances from a Yuhan Hoesa, provided the underlying transaction is documented and reported through a designated foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions, however, are subject to a prior report or approval regime. A non-resident shareholder injecting equity into a Korean LLC must file a capital transaction report through the domestic bank or via the Korea Exchange Information System. Once the equity is registered, dividend remittances are treated as current account invisibles and can be wired abroad with a standard tax withholding certificate. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds; Korean entities are permitted to hold foreign currency in domestic bank foreign currency accounts indefinitely, but proceeds from exports must be collected within six months from the date of export unless an extension is granted. Practical hurdles for profit remittance include the need to prove the absence of outstanding tax arrears, submission of audited financial statements if paid-in capital exceeds statutory thresholds, and the 'substance over form' review by the bank to confirm the distribution does not violate capital preservation rules. The Bank of Korea periodically monitors net foreign currency positions, and banks enforce transaction-level health checks to deter money laundering. Overall, the won is highly convertible for bona fide trade and service flows, but all crossings must be accompanied by purpose codes and supporting contracts to satisfy the reporting engine.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 32 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the related Enforcement Decree, Korean exporters must collect export proceeds within 6 months from the exportation date (Korean customs clearance or service completion date, whichever is applicable). Extension is allowed for up to 12 months with bank approval and up to 24 months with a BOK report. There is no mandatory conversion into Korean won; proceeds may be credited to a foreign currency account with a registered bank, but the full amount must be repatriated, not left offshore, and the receiving bank must be notified with supporting invoices and bills of lading (or delivery confirmations for cloud kitchen supply contracts) to generate the outward/ inward foreign exchange report. Failure to repatriate within the timeline results in administrative penalties and possible criminal sanctions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low - Not legally viable for domestic Korean settlement. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK FCA-authorized e-money institutions, EU EMI licenses, or US fintech BaaS platforms) are not authorized to open virtual IBANs or provide KRW clearing on behalf of a Korean-domiciled LLC. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires all local currency settlements and foreign exchange conversions to flow through a foreign exchange bank licensed in Korea. Foreign EMIs cannot report capital transactions, cannot issue Korean purpose codes, and cannot interface with the Bank of Korea's reporting systems. They may only serve as an auxiliary foreign-currency collection tool for non-Korean sales, but even that requires entering into a cross-border payment arrangement with a domestic bank, which defeats the purpose. Therefore, a Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a primary relationship with a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank. No grain of legal workaround exists for ghost kitchen payouts from UberEats or door-to-door aggregators; those payouts must be received in KRW through domestic acquiring and settlement rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory director (and any person holding 10% or more equity) must appear physically at a Korean bank branch for initial KYC interview if the director is not an existing banking customer. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for a domestic LLC deposit account with transaction authority. However, for high-grade foreign investors, some banks allow a 'dual visit' arrangement where the first face-to-face interview is completed at the bank's overseas branch or via a video call pre-registered with the local branch, followed by the physical delivery of original corporate documents by the company's local representative attorney. The bank's compliance department retains the right to require a second physical interview at the main branch in Seoul. In practice, a non-resident sole director must either fly to Seoul with a company chop (corporate seal), certificate of incorporation, and passport, or appoint a local Korean resident as a joint signatory with strict mandate limitations. We recommend a physical presence visit to Shinhan or KEB Hana's corporate banking center in Seoul to avoid onboarding delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained beneficial ownership chains involving a non-resident parent shell company in a tax-neutral or high-secrecy jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full organizational chart from ultimate individual beneficial owner down to the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, notarized certificates of good standing, apostilled certificates of incorporation for each intermediate entity, bank reference letters from each intermediary's home bank, and sworn affidavits from all directors detailing the source of funds for the equity injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of 'ghost kitchen' revenue comingling with unlicensed food manufacturing or underreported cash sales.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The entity's Korean Food Sanitation Act license (business license for food service), each virtual brand's franchise or licensing agreement, a formal delivery aggregator settlement statement from UberEats and DoorDash showing net payouts by brand, monthly GST/VAT returns filed with the National Tax Service, and a CPA-issued report confirming that all payout accounts are company-owned and no personal cash envelopes are used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concerns about tax residency mismatch, where the LLC claims effective management outside Korea to shift corporate profits, while all kitchen operations occur in Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed transfer pricing documentation package for the virtual brands, including a master file and local file (if applicable), an analysis under Article 5 of the Korea International Tax Adjustment Act, lease agreements for the ghost kitchen facilities in Korea, utility bills, payroll records for Korean employees, board meeting minutes held in Seoul, and an independent tax opinion confirming that the LLC is a Korean tax resident subject to 9-24% corporate tax.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious FX flow pattern where the initial capital is denominated exclusively in a high-risk currency (e.g., cryptocurrency-converted USD) and arrives from unrelated third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital subscription agreement, bank statements from the remitting bank showing the beneficial owner's name matching the shareholder registry, certified copies of the overseas investor's passport, a source-of-wealth explanation supported by audited financial statements or employment records, and a legal declaration that the funds are not derived from gambling, darknet markets, or any activity listed as money laundering predicates under the Proceeds of Crime Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial capital contribution from a non-resident shareholder must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 using the explicit purpose code 'A100 - Equity investment (non-financial)' under the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System. The receiving domestic bank will verify the remitter's name against the shareholder register, issue a Certificate of Foreign Exchange Transaction, and report the transaction to the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Within 30 days of the remittance, the Korean entity must file a capital investment report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance or complete an automated report through the receiving bank. The capital verification process requires the external auditor or certified public accountant to reconcile the SWIFT receipt, the bank's credit advice, and the board resolution approving the share issuance. For a Yuhan Hoesa with no minimum capital requirement, the injected funds may be used immediately for kitchen deposits, equipment purchases, and payroll once the bank confirms the purpose code and the 'alien investment' free-conversion route is approved. If the shareholder uses a non-Korean intermediary, the bank will apply enhanced due diligence and request a full chain of custody to ensure no third-party settlement risk.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of raw ingredient imports, packaging supplies, and franchise technology royalties, the Korean LLC should use a SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers under purpose code 'B210 - Import payments' or 'B310 - Royalties and license fees'. For high-value or recurring trade flows, a Documentary Collection (DP/DA) or Irrevocable Confirmed Letter of Credit issued by a Korean Tier-1 bank is preferred, especially when importing specialized kitchen machinery from Japan or the United States. Local supplier payments (rent, utility, third-party delivery fleet fees) are cleared through the domestic Banking Payment Network (BOK-Wire+ and CD/ATM switch), using standard KFTC account transfers with settlement messages. DoorDash and UberEats payouts are received in KRW through the platform's Korean acquiring arm, typically via a daily electronic settlement message directly into the operating account; the bank reconciles those against the Delivery Aggregator Settlement Report. For cross-border royalty outbound remittances, the bank will require the corresponding trademark/patent registration certificate, the license agreement stamped with a negotiation date, and withholding tax clearance from the National Tax Service. All outbound wires over USD 10,000 require mandatory foreign exchange reporting and are checked against the UN sanctions list and FATF watchlists in real time.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank up to 12 months tenor, covering declared USD/ KRW or EUR/ KRW exposure from projected ingredient import invoices and aggregator net settlements; physical delivery is mandatory and unused forward portions must be reversed by maturity.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are strictly limited to non-resident financial counterparties under Korean regulations; a domestic LLC is generally barred from entering NDFs unless it proves to the Bank of Korea that it maintains a genuine underlying foreign-currency asset or liability not eligible for physical delivery.

Cross-currency swaps are permitted for synthetic KRW funding when the shareholder lends USD to the LLC and swaps the principal/interest into KRW, provided the swap is executed through a domestic foreign exchange bank and reported as a capital transaction; no exotic option products are allowed for treasury-only speculation.

Plain vanilla FX options with zero-premium collars are allowed for hedging against a sudden KRW appreciation on the USD-denominated future payouts from UberEats Global and DoorDash US, but the bank requires a written treasury policy approved by the LLC's board and a mitigation analysis demonstrating that the collars reduce, not enlarge, the firm's FX VaR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Business Place Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar year entity, by March 31 of the following calendar year; an extension to June 30 is available upon prior application to NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 0.03% per day on unpaid tax, capped at 75%; underreporting penalty 10% and omission penalty 20% of attributed tax; continued delinquency may lead to enforced tax collection and administrative cancellation of business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Income Tax Surcharge Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local taxation authority (Si, Gun or Gu office) via Korea Local Tax System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the national corporate income tax return; due by March 31 (or June 30 if national deadline extended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local income tax surcharge accrues 0.03% daily penalty up to a 75% ceiling, plus local tax delinquency charges; failure to file may lead to seizure of bank accounts and cancellation of the local business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Adoption of Audited Financial Statements and Statutory Reports
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Yuhan Hoesa as shown in the register of members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within 6 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar year entity, no later than June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM within the statutory window subjects each director to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million; any dividend declared without adopted financial statements may be void and recoverable; prolonged failure may be treated as a material governance breach enabling court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Company Report (if foreign shareholding exists in the Yuhan Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) acting as the administrative body for the Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the last day of February for the preceding calendar year; newly registered foreign investment companies file first report in the year after registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 3 million for failure to file or for false reporting; persistent non-compliance may result in cancellation of foreign-investment tax incentives or accelerated exit procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Companies, an independent certified public accountant audit is compulsory when the entity’s total assets are KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million) or more, OR annual sales are KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million) or more, OR the average number of regular employees exceeds 300. Entities meeting any of these triggers must appoint a licensed external auditor and file audited financial statements in accordance with the statutory framework.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies meeting the above audit thresholds or listed status; for non-public Yuhan Hoesa entities, Korean SMEs Accounting Standards (KAS SMEs) may be applied, but K-IFRS is mandatory where the entity is publicly accountable or meets statutory audit thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea operates a 30-day event-driven beneficial ownership reporting system. Any transfer of membership or change in direct or indirect beneficial ownership must be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit within 30 days of the change. The company must update its register of members at the annual general meeting and maintain an up-to-date beneficial ownership map at the registered office; there is no separate annual re-filing unless a reportable event has occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (member register or Sawon Myungbu)
Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors (if any)
Minutes of Shareholders General Meetings and Board of Directors Meetings
Accounting ledgers and supporting vouchers kept under Article 29 of the Korean Commercial Act
Register of Charges or Mortgages (only to the extent the company has created security over its assets)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% national corporate income tax (plus 10% local income surtax, resulting in a combined top marginal rate of 27.5% for annual taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays for foreign-invested high-tech ventures in Korean Free Economic Zones; reduced statutory rates for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; R&D tax credits; temporary investment tax credits for facility investment; special deductions for job creation and vocational training; exemption or reduction for qualifying green-energy infrastructure projects.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세 과세표준 및 세액 신고서) filed via the HomeTax electronic filing system (https://www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a mandatory mid-term prepayment (interim self-assessment) for the first six months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by March 31 for a December 31 year-end). An extension of up to one month may be granted in accordance with the Framework Act on National Taxes, but any tax due remains payable by the original statutory deadline unless separate payment extension is approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, business registration number (business license number), tax identification number, fiscal year start and end dates, registered address, tax office jurisdiction, and industry classification code (ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean-resident entity owned by non-residents, state the foreign shareholder names, tax residency countries, and percentage of direct/indirect shareholding. Indicate whether any the equity structure triggers beneficial ownership documentation for treaty purposes. Do NOT enter a foreign branch number; the company is a domestic corporation and must file as a Korean resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue computation: total sales from delivery-only food services, virtual brand licensing fees, platform commission reimbursements, and any other operating income. Include returns, allowances, and discounts as deductions to arrive at net revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue must be recorded in Korean won. For cross-border virtual brand trademark royalties received by the Korean entity from affiliated foreign brand owners, treat as operating revenue and concurrently verify whether a withholding tax obligation arises for outgoing royalty payments. If the Korean entity operates as a limited-risk logistics or distribution hub for intangible-bearing transactions, adjust revenue under the arm's length principle and attach transfer pricing schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable and exempt income: dividend income from qualifying domestic subsidiaries, certain gains on disposal of assets acquired under government incentives, and statutorily exempt contributions. Value-added tax collected is excluded from revenue and not reported in the corporate income tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only statutory exemptions under the Corporate Income Tax Act and the Restriction of Special Taxation Act may be claimed. Foreign tax credits and treaty exclusions are NOT to be entered here – they belong in the tax credit section. Ensure that any claim to exemption is supported by certificates from the relevant authorities; otherwise, the National Tax Service (NTS) will reclassify the item as taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and non-deductible items: cost of goods sold (raw food ingredients, packaging), wages, rent, utilities, fuel, insurance, depreciation, marketing, delivery expenses, and other ordinary and necessary business expenses. Add back non-deductible entertainment expenses exceeding statutory limits, late taxes, penalties, certain donations, and amounts disallowed due to lack of business substance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any management, service, or royalty fees paid to non-resident related parties must satisfy the fair market value / arm's length standard. Korean tax law disallows deductions for payments to related entities unless the services were actually rendered and benefit the Korean operating business. Such cross-border payments are also subject to withholding taxes (see profit repatriation). Pay strict attention to thin capitalization rules (maximum debt-to-equity ratio of 3:1 for foreign-controlled Korean companies) to avoid interest deduction disallowance. Financial statements and accounting records must clearly demonstrate the ghost kitchen operational expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculation: begin with Box 2 gross revenue, subtract Box 3 exempt income and Box 4 deductible expenses, and then apply losses carried forward (10-year statutory period) and special statutory deductions to arrive at taxable income before application of tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-sourced income is taxable to the Korean resident entity on its worldwide income. If the Korean entity is actually a branch or permanent establishment (PE) of a foreign corporation (which would be confirmed at Box 1), only Korean-source income would be included. Loss carryforwards must satisfy the continuity-of-business test and be supported by audited accounts. The tax return must reconcile taxable income from the GAAP financial statements using a reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax liability and credits: apply the progressive corporate tax rates (10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 22% on income between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion; 25% on income exceeding KRW 300 billion). Add 10% local income surtax. Apply tax credits for R&D, investment, foreign tax paid, employment, and any other statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits for taxes paid by the Korean entity on its worldwide income, limited to the Korean tax attributable to foreign-source income. Prepayments made during the year (interim tax) are credited in this box, and a final balance due or refund is calculated. If the Korean entity has non-resident shareholders, the withholding tax on any dividend distribution is NOT deducted here – it is a separate withholding obligation handled at the time of distribution. Any tax treaty benefits available to a foreign parent are claimed at the withholding level, not in this corporate return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, interim taxes, and final settlement: declare amounts paid through the mid-term prepayment schedule, payroll withholding, and other advance tax payments; compute the net amount due to the NTS or the refundable amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure interim prepayments are accurate; underpayment leads to statutory interest. Refunds for resident companies with foreign shareholders may be subject to additional scrutiny and administrative delay, so consider offsetting against other tax liabilities. If the taxpayer expects a large refund, file the Form 32-1 (refund request) separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary attachments: list related-party transactions, financial statements, balance sheet, profit and loss account, transfer pricing forms (master file, local file, CbCR), and any other compulsory schedules such as foreign account reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete all required attachment schedules in the HomeTax electronic portal. For cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion, attach a TP Local File and Master File. The Country-by-Country Report threshold of KRW 1 trillion in group turnover requires separate filing through the NTS e-CbCR system. Failure to attach these documents materially increases audit risk and penalty exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 20% of the unpaid tax for cases of mere non-filing, and 40% where the non-filing is consequence of omission or underreporting of income (Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes). Late payment surcharge: 0.022% per day of delay applied to the unpaid tax amount (Article 47-3). Failure to submit required transfer pricing documentation attracts a penalty of up to 20-30% of the amount of transaction adjustment under Article 11 of the International Tax Adjustment Act. Criminal tax evasion (willful and with intent to evade) triggers imprisonment for up to 2 years or a fine not exceeding five times the evaded amount (Act on Punishment of Tax Evaders); aggravated cases involving tax evasion exceeding KRW 500 million may lead to imprisonment up to 5 years. Fraudulent withholding failures incur penalties of 1% of the unwithheld amount per month. In addition, the competent authorities may impose a travel ban (blacklisting) on responsible directors and block bank accounts.
